reformulation: Exact option-index compression of a menu/packing model. 13,550 binaries sit in 627 disjoint at-most-one rows (oneblpline, RHS 1); partitioning each group by its complete frequency coefficient vector yields exactly 1,254 blocks (two per group) whose options j=0..N satisfy a_b+j*d_b in every one of the 43 capacity coefficients and c_b+j*e_b in cost, with constant frequency coefficients and positive steps. Each block becomes one binary activation y and one bounded general integer index k with 0<=k<=N, k<=N*y; the 627 packing rows become sum_b y_b <= 1, the 46 frequency and 43 capacity definition rows become 92 lower/upper and 43 lower inequalities, and the 90 continuous auxiliaries (including obj and defblpobj) are substituted away. 13,640 vars / 717 rows -> 2,508 vars (1,254 binary + 1,254 integer) / 2,016 rows; 191,947 -> 33,494 nonzeros. The agent states the LP aggregate image is unchanged, i.e. compression, not strengthening, and claims no runtime gain (both models hit the solver time limit).
claim_class: Objective-preserving integer bijection (4 claims x 2,508 affine projection coordinates, objective Equal) plus one explicit complete-domain bijection pair {forward_claim 0, reverse_claim 1}: integer modes are claims 0-1, claims 2-3 carry the aggregate LP image with both integrality flags off. Beyond projection the pair owns a full 2,508-coordinate target right-inverse list and 13,640-coordinate doubled-source injectivity including the 90 continuous auxiliaries; no LP point bijection and no strictness claim.
claims: 4 claims, each with 2,508 affine_projection entries and objective 'Equal': (0) forward, input+output integrality true; (1) reverse, both true; (2) forward, both false; (3) reverse, both false (cases/test60/request.json; literals at tools/prepare_menus.py:27-30).

One bijection, written as claims[]-indexed {'forward_claim':0,'reverse_claim':1} in the request but assembled from a different key spelling {'claim':pair,'injectivity':unique} at tools/prepare_menu_cases.py:19.

Bijection duties: the reverse lift re-appends every target coordinate as a right-inverse obligation (checks.extend(menu_laws[j] for j in range(len(target['vars']))) = 2,508 refs, tools/menu_lift_prepare.py:55-57), and injectivity is a separate 13,640-equality object (tools/menu_injectivity.py:35-95).

Kernel census of the accepted certificate: 112,210 terminal obligations = 52,051 in the three ordinary Return bodies (12,049/9,541/30,461) + 46,519 in the single MenuLift + 13,640 injectivity equalities; 67,750 branches, menu_lifts 1, flow/interval lifts 0 (cases/test60/preparation.json verify stdout).

agent_manual_work: Two independent hand-written MPS readers over all 207,051 lines / 15,698,417 bytes: a token/section parser with explicit marker, bound and duplicate checks, and a regex extractor, both using exact Fraction conversion and asserted equal on rows, coefficients, RHS, bounds and INTORG pairs (digest transcript, evals 2 and 6).

The structural discovery itself, done in eval code: 627 packing groups, the 1,254 blocks obtained by partitioning each group by its complete frequency coefficient vector, and all 13,550 options checked against a_b+j*d_b and c_b+j*e_b (1,219,500 progression comparisons recorded in cases/test60/menu_structure.json).

Three hypotheses rejected with the numbers that killed them: all 13,550 non-cost columns are distinct; capacity-gcd contiguity fails on 627 of 1,254 blocks because frequency-two capacities step by 2 (fixed by using the option index); all 627 groups form one resource-incidence component (report 'Rejected or inconclusive approaches').

top_capability: BATCH_TEMPLATES - a compact, kernel-expanded representation for families of homogeneous rule instances. The whole test60 finding is 1,254 menus that differ only in their option list and index range, yet the certificate spells out 13,550 generated variables, 2,508 generated rows and 46,519 menu obligations, which is what makes the RPA 122,979,323 B (45.8% of the text cap) for a reformulation the analysis agent produced in 12 turns, 280.4 s and 0 failed calls. The same batch shape, with the MenuLift/bijunction constructors of RULE_BUILDERS underneath it, is what makes the shared test59 sibling cheap to re-derive.
notes: Which side to optimise: the proof side. Agent side: 12 turns, 11 tool calls, 0 failures, 151,201 tokens, 280.4 s wall (276.0 s LLM), and the finding fits in 1,587,402 B of audit.json (1,027,382 B block table). Proof side: 1,115 lines of preparer across 8 files, RPA 122,979,323 B / RPX 90,516,456 B, 112,210 obligations, 67,750 branches, 52.65 s preparation, 164.73 s replay + 5 attacks; checking is cheap in release (execute 5.36 s, work 39,126,580 = 3.9% of 1e9, peak live facts 13,640 of 1e6) and 12.7x slower in debug, so the cost is certificate size and construction volume, not verification. Obligation split: 52,051 ordinary Return + 46,519 single MenuLift + 13,640 injectivity. Sibling test59 (same generator, 13 turns, 338 s) behaves identically (160,289 obligations, work 38,506,669, verify 4.05 s, RPA 129,299,645 B), so these needs are the menu family's, not test60's alone. No solver evidence exists either way: original and reformulated both reached the time limit (4567.94 s vs 4613.30 s), so the claim rests entirely on the algebraic certificate. NOTE: the ~121 MB remainder of the RPA beyond the 1,832,200 B claims half is inferred as the block structure (MenuLift body + injectivity + 3 Return bodies).
